title: Ground surveys from 2002-2017 confirm steady TESS apsidal drifts in eight tidal binaries and a non-tidal 21-year rate in TIC 444544588, but cannot test four other circumbinary-planet candidates
abstract: Question: do the TESS apsidal drifts of the Thornton et al. (2026) circumbinary-planet candidates continue in independent pre-TESS data? Method: we measured the primary-to-secondary eclipse time D in 92 chunks of ASAS-3 (2000-2009), SuperWASP DR1 (2004-2008), ASAS-SN (2013-2025) and ZTF light curves of 25 eccentric eclipsing binaries, with the TESS eclipse shapes of a prior campaign study. We compared D with TESS-only predictions from the exact eclipse geometry; the drift ratio kappa is 1 for a steady drift and 0 for no drift before TESS. Results: eight binaries where tides explain the rate give kappa = 1.014 +- 0.032 (chi-square 5.1 for 7 dof); in TIC 56023695, D was 486 +- 18 min larger in 2002. In TIC 444544588, ASAS-3 data from 2005 give D 226 +- 14 min smaller than in TESS (prediction 208 min; kappa = 1.08 +- 0.14). Its 21-year apsidal rate is 39 (33-45) x 1e-3 deg per cycle, which needs an apsidal constant k2 near 10 if tides cause it. Thus a non-tidal cause acts; a planet would need an unstable orbit, so a stellar or brown-dwarf companion is probable. For the four other excess candidates the ground data have little power: TIC 146204045 kappa = 1.2 +- 1.2, TIC 123951716 0.1 +- 0.8, TIC 399127035 -1.3 +- 1.1, TIC 82893635 undetermined. A mid-eclipse timing screen shows an 88 +- 17 min offset of TIC 146204045 in 2005 (a massive third body) and a 29-42 min offset of TIC 291751499 in SuperWASP data. Limitations: sparse ground sampling of long-period binaries, fixed eclipse shapes, an ASAS-SN time-stamp offset of about 5 min (D is not sensitive to it), and order-of-magnitude third-body estimates.
